assumptions.claim: The FSM state register is only assigned values from the enumerated pad_st_e set.
assumptions.risk: An illegal state value could cause the FSM to enter undefined behavior, skipping critical padding steps or leaking data.

assumptions.claim: The mux_sel_e signal never takes on values outside {MuxNone, MuxFifo, MuxPrefix, MuxFuncPad, MuxZeroEnd} (binary 5-7).
assumptions.risk: Illegal select values may activate unintended data sources, potentially exposing internal state or causing incorrect pad data.

assumptions.claim: The parameter KeccakCountW matches the address width expected by the Keccak round module.
assumptions.cond: When block_addr_limit is used for address generation.
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch can lead to out-of-bounds memory access, incomplete block processing, or pad corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The pad_st_e state encodings are not documented; they may be sparse for fault tolerance but no error handling for unused 7‑bit values is defined in this declaration.
uncertain_points.cond: If a soft error flips a state bit.
uncertain_points.risk: An undefined FSM state could bypass pad10*1 or flush operations, compromising integrity or security of the hash.

uncertain_points.claim: mux_sel_e defines only 5 valid values, leaving three encodings unused. It is unclear whether downstream mux logic provides a safe default.
uncertain_points.cond: If mux_sel_e becomes 5–7 due to a logic error or radiation event.
uncertain_points.risk: Unintended data selection may propagate internal secrets or corrupt pad data.
